newsitem.title: CHINA: INTERVIEW-China Light has ambitious plans in China.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-China Light has ambitious plans in China.

text.p: China Light & Power Co Ltd said on Wednesday it has ambitious plans for its development in China but that earnings contribution from the mainland was far from significant.
"We will expand as much as we can," managing director Ross Sayers told Reuters in an interview. "We are quite ambitious."

The sale earlier this year of a 20 percent China Light stake to CITIC Pacific Ltd had given the Hong Kong utility both a powerful partner in China and cash to invest further on the mainland, Sayers said.
CITIC Pacific, the Hong Kong-listed arm of China's state trading giant China International Trust and Investment Corp, bought the stake for HK$16.25 billion.
"Having a strategic association with a major PRC (People's Republic of China) enterprise was important for our future," said Sayers.
"We believe CITIC to be the best possible choice and we are delighted with the association. We think the association to be very beneficial when we look to our future in China."

CITIC Pacific's move is considered by analysts to be part of a move by mainland companies to become more involved in Hong Kong's strategic industries. Hong Kong returned to Chinese rule on July 1 after 156 years as a British colony.
Sayers said having a Chinese partner was "very helpful" in developing business on the mainland, "particularly if you are quite ambitious".

The partnership has already yielded results, with four years of negotiations on a power plant project in China's Shandong province finally resulting in a joint venture agreement in May between China Light's China Energy Investment Co Ltd, Shandong Electric Power Co, Shandong International Trust and Investment Corp and Electricite de France International SA.
Sayers said CITIC Pacific was "quietly helpful" in giving guidance on how to proceed with projects to develop power plants in Shandong province.

China Light & Power also signed a joint venture agreement in April with Exxon Energy Ltd, Shenzhen Qianwan Electric Power Development Co Ltd, Guangdong Electric Power Holdings Co and Kanematsu Power (South China) Co Ltd to develop a 1,050-megawatt gas-fired power plan in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen.

Sayers declined to disclose any new projects China Light was considering in China but said the utility had more than HK$16 billion in cash which it could spend on projects on the mainland and elsewhere in Asia.
"We have developed a strategy and we are trying to find projects to fit the strategy," he said.
But the contribution from China would take a long time to have an impact on China Light's earnings, said Sayers.
"We are looking to buy existing assets for current earnings," he said.
China Light's earnings still "overwhelmingly" came from Hong Kong, where expectations of higher economic growth rates in the future made the company optimistic about the market, said Sayers.
"Hong Kong's future is assured and it will be increasingly a gateway into China," he said.
